reasoning: Both sets are disciplined and buildable, and each misses a different user requirement. Set A has the stronger quant design. Every stage starts with a synthetic known-answer check: S2's SYNTH checks and S3's FSYN planted-feature check. S3 has a registered holdout that can run only once, with family-wise correction and a stated detectable effect. Each null-hypothesis-testing handoff names exactly what the skill receives. A also covers the full S1 cross-check: yahooquery, the user's 10-delisted reference check (CHECK-09) and threshold calibration with data-analysis. Its walking skeleton is a true vertical slice: start a download from the app, watch it live, explore the result. A frontend-design direction-approval task gates every view. Every stage after S1 opens with a synthetic skeleton milestone that later milestones build on. A's main gaps: it defers the PPO agents to a later idea, rules out the rented GPU ('Cloud compute; every model trains on the user's machine'), carries a stale AGENTS.md and an S1-only brief, and is verbose. Set B covers all four stages, including PPO agents and GPU bundles. Its shared walk-forward engine, hypothesis ledger and lockbox are clean, and its task packets carry concrete golden-case oracles. But B drops the yahooquery cross-check and the user's 10-name delisted list entirely, adds FRED and EDGAR sources the user never asked for, and leaves the feature list undefined. Its S2 has no synthetic skeleton and starts directly on real data. M8 lumps forecast portfolios, agents and the verdict into one milestone. B's frontend-design use is thin, and its packets point to a CONSTRAINTS.md that isn't in the set. On balance, A's tighter methodology and milestones narrowly outweigh B's wider stage coverage.
